column3: The annex heading, "Annex F (normative) Discipline resolution methods", with no text of its own before F.1; its content is F.1-F.2.2. Positive: hierarchy_resolution.va (runs; the leaf discipline reaches the top segment).

Discipline resolution is described in 7.4; it provides the semantics for two methods of resolving the discipline of undeclared interconnect. This annex provides a possible algorithm for achieving the semantics of each method. It is also possible to develop and use other algorithms to match the semantics. The algorithm is the implementation's choice so long as 7.4's semantics hold. Positive: hierarchy_resolution.va.

The undeclared nets are resolved at each level of the hierarchy in which continuous (analog) has precedence over discrete (digital). ... A net segment of a signal on the upper connection of a port shall be considered as the parent to a net segment on the lower connection of the port. ... When a signal is being traversed depth-first, this means that the traversal shall start at the bottom (leaf) net segments. Definitions of parent/child and of the two traversal orders; the errors are F.2.1's and F.2.2's (see header). Positive: hierarchy_resolution.va.
